chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the people take their places in Mina, a Caller calls out on behalf of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'If you are intending for Me to be Pleased, so I am Pleased'.

key_terms.مَوَاطِنَهُمْ: their places/stations (referring to where pilgrims settle)
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a sacred site near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What does the divine Caller announce to pilgrims in Mina during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, the Imam (AS) describes a divine announcement made as pilgrims take their stations in Mina, signifying that Allah’s pleasure is contingent upon their sincere desire for it. This highlights the Shia theological emphasis on the reciprocity between human intention (niyyah) and divine grace, suggesting that the acceptance of Hajj is not merely ritualistic but deeply rooted in the pilgrim's conscious seeking of God's approval.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hajjal, from Dawood Bin Abu Yazeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘When the people take their places in Mina, a Caller calls out on behalf of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic: ‘If you are intending for Me<sup>azwj</sup> to be Pleased, so I<sup>asws</sup> am Pleased’.
en.sarwar: 41. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that no other journey affects one’s flesh, blood, skin and hair more than the journey to Makkah. No one reaches it (the journey) without facing hardships.’”
